title: SDK Integration Walkthrough - Aurora Tech
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Aurora Tech through Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts, auth and env setup, and discussed hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs. Customer asked clarifying questions about API key rotation, SSO/KMS, latency/cost tuning and requested security docs and a repo with examples. Agreed next steps: share sample repo, security pack, pricing sheet, and schedule a POC benchmark run for early December.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aurora Tech Eng Mgr), Liam O'Neill (Aurora BE), Priya Kapoor (Aurora Security)

00:00 - Jasmine Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jasmine from Redwood, and with me is Diego from our solutions engineering team. quick agenda, we'll walk through our Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts, auth and env setup, then dig into deployment options and security questions.
00:18 - Maya Chen: Hi thanks, excited. We're mainly looking to integrate embeddings and chat for our support triage flow, and want to understand the fastest way to get a PoC up.
00:33 - Diego Morales: Great. we'll start with the python quickstart. basically pip install redwood-sdk, export REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment, and call client.generate(...) or client.chat.stream for streaming responses. small note: the env var name in the sample is REDWOOD_API_KEY but we also show a config file pattern if you rotate keys via KMS.
01:05 - Liam O'Neill: when you say rotate via KMS, do you mean we can plug our cloud KMS and Redwood will use customer-managed keys?
01:12 - Diego Morales: yes, for Private deployments we support integrating with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. for Hosted we manage keys but you can use envelope encryption with your KMS in some enterprise plans. I'll drop the docs after.
01:45 - Priya Kapoor: are you SOC 2 and ISO certified? we need audit artifacts and, like, audit logs for token-level access.
01:52 - Jasmine Park: we are SOC 2 Type II, and we have an audit pack — Diego will share the security packet that includes SOC 2 attestation, ISO references, SSO SAML integration notes and audit log formats.
02:10 - Diego Morales: moving on, TypeScript quickstart: npm install @redwood-ai/sdk, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or use a .env file with dotenv. sample code shows client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-medium', messages: [...] }). watch for streaming differences between node fetch and browser fetch.
02:45 - Maya Chen: any special setup for browser vs server? our FE team wants a browser example but we plan to proxy through a backend for auth.
02:52 - Diego Morales: recommend proxying through your backend to avoid exposing API keys. we also have short-lived session tokens and BFF patterns in the docs for safe browser usage.
03:15 - Liam O'Neill: what's the typical latency and token cost for chat? our SLA target is <300ms p50 for single-turn short prompts.
03:25 - Diego Morales: depends on model and deployment. hosted medium models are usually 150-350ms p50 on our hosted tier for 512-token requests; for <300ms consistently you'll want Dedicated or Private pinned capacity and some batching and cache settings disabled for low-latency access. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching config to hit cost/latency tradeoffs.
03:55 - Maya Chen: can you explain Optimize a little more?
04:00 - Jasmine Park: sure, Optimize is our toolkit that analyzes your workload and recommends batching, cache, and quantization profiles. Diego: example?
04:07 - Diego Morales: for inference-heavy endpoints we suggest prefix caching for re-used contexts, and dynamic batching with max latency window 20ms to hit throughput. the tool also suggests model variants — e.g., redwood-chat-small for cheaper replies or an fp16 quantized variant for Dedicated. all recommendations are in the Console under Optimize -> Recommendations.
04:40 - Priya Kapoor: from a security perspective, we need VPC peering or a Private control plane. what's supported?
04:48 - Diego Morales: we offer Private (VPC) deployments and on-prem options. private control plane with customer-managed networking, and you can restrict egress/ingress. also support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC in Console.
05:15 - Maya Chen: ok, let's go through a live demo of the Python quickstart in the repo.
05:20 - Diego Morales: I'll share screen — code snippet:
05:30 - Diego Morales: from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient
05:34 - Diego Morales: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
05:40 - Diego Morales: resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-chat-medium', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Summarize support ticket 12345'}])
05:47 - Maya Chen: nice. when you call client.chat.create, does that stream tokens?
05:51 - Diego Morales: you can call client.chat.stream(...) for streaming. in python we show an iterator pattern. TypeScript shows an async iterable or callback. streaming behavior is slightly different across runtimes and there are small transcript mismatches in the auto-generated sdk docs occasionally, but the samples are tested.
06:20 - Liam O'Neill: about auth rotation — if we rotate keys everyday, is there a way to automate without deploying config changes?
06:28 - Diego Morales: yes, we support short-lived tokens and we have a token-issuance endpoint; typical pattern is BFF exchanges your long-lived credential for short-lived session token which is used by clients. also our SDK supports reading from metadata servers for in-cloud keys.
06:50 - Maya Chen: can you show the .env example and how we manage multiple environments (staging/prod)?
06:55 - Diego Morales: sure, we suggest .env files per environment: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-prod-..., REDWOOD_ENV=production; and in code load via dotenv. For CI we recommend injecting secrets via your CI secret store and not checking .env into git.
07:30 - Jasmine Park: quick interruption — pricing note: for hosted we charge per token; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit; we'll send a sizing estimate once you share traffic profile.
07:45 - Maya Chen: we'll share traffic shape in the next action item.
08:00 - Diego Morales: switching to Console walkthrough — Console shows per-route cost and latency breakdowns, and Optimize recommendations for model configs. you can create rollout policies (canary/A-B) and automatic fallbacks if a model variant fails.
08:35 - Liam O'Neill: if a model variant fails during a rollout, does it automatically fallback to another zone or model?
08:39 - Diego Morales: yes, routing policies let you fallback to a compatible variant or region; there's a priority list and health checks govern failover.
09:00 - Priya Kapoor: what about audit logs and token-level tracing for compliance?
09:05 - Diego Morales: Console retains traces with request IDs; enterprise plans include longer retention and S3 export. logs include model, route, token counts, and user_id metadata you pass.
09:30 - Maya Chen: let's talk POC scope — we want to test embeddings for support search and chat for auto-summarization under our traffic shape. target is 1k concurrent users peak.
09:45 - Diego Morales: for 1k concurrent users we typically recommend Dedicated with autoscaling and a burst pool, or Private if you need network isolation. we'll size GPUs based on sequence length and qps; send the sample workload and we'll run a benchmark.
10:10 - Jasmine Park: agreed next steps: we'll share a sample repo, security docs, and a pricing estimate. any other questions on SDKs?
10:18 - Liam O'Neill: one more, TypeScript streaming in the browser, do you support SSE or web sockets?
10:24 - Diego Morales: we support server-sent events and websocket proxies in the SDK. for browsers we typically use event-stream via BFF.
10:40 - Maya Chen: ok that's helpful.
10:45 - Diego Morales: couple of transcript artifacts — in some auto-generated docs model names are mis-typed (e.g., Redwood Optimize sometimes shows 'Redwood Opti' in older docs). sorry for any confusion. we'll ensure the repo has corrected up-to-date samples.
11:10 - Jasmine Park: recap: Jasmine sends sample repo and pricing; Diego sends security pack and KMS notes; Maya provides traffic profile and success criteria; we schedule POC benchmark for week of Dec 7.
11:28 - Maya Chen: sounds good. thanks everyone.
11:32 - Priya Kapoor: thanks, we'll review security docs and come back with any questions.
11:40 - Liam O'Neill: thanks Diego, the code walkthrough was helpful, we'll try the quickstart today.
11:48 - Jasmine Park: great, I'll follow up with the links and next steps in email.
12:00 - End of recording.

Note: transcription contains occasional misheard words (e.g., 'Redwood Opti' or 'redwood-chat-medium' mis-typed) and speaker overlaps. References to shared artifacts: sample repo link (will be shared), security pack link (to be shared), pricing spreadsheet (to be shared).
